title: Imaging Mass Cytometry Antibody Staining
author: Michelle Daniel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfz8jp9w
materials: Log use of dewaxing robot in log sheet
During washing, prepare Ir-intercalator solution (50 μL/Sample).
Dip slides with stained samples briefly in ddH2O.

steps.title: Run dewaxing robot
steps.instruction: Execute the dewaxing robot program on the unstained slides.

substeps.instruction: Allow unstained samples to equilibrate to room temperature for at least 10 min.
Transport the samples to the dewaxing robot.
Record robot usage in the log sheet.
Verify reagent levels; refresh any reagent that has been in use >5 days or used >5 times.
Press the button to lift the sample‑holder arm, load the slides into the slideholder, and place the slideholder in the sample holder.
Select program 1 on the robot.
Start the program.
When the program finishes, press the button to lift the arm and transfer the slideholder with slides into a tray containing TBS buffer.
Perform all actions inside a fume hood.

steps.title: Heat‑induced epitope retrieval
steps.instruction: Perform HIER in the decloaking chamber at 95 °C for 30 min.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 mL ddH₂O to the decloaking chamber.
Fill all unused cuvettes with 200 mL ddH₂O and each cuvette that will be used with 200 mL HIER buffer.
Select the 30‑min, 95 °C protocol and start heating the chamber.
When the temperature reaches 95 °C, a prompt appears; open the pressure chamber carefully.
Place the slideholder (from step 1) into the tray containing HIER buffer inside the pressure chamber.
Incubate at 95 °C for exactly 30 min.
After incubation, open the pressure chamber, place the tray with the slideholder on the bench at room temperature, and allow to cool for 20 min.
Transfer the slides from the tray into TBS buffer.

steps.title: Apply barrier and block
steps.instruction: Circle tissue sections with a hydrophobic barrier pen and block.

substeps.instruction: Remove one slide from TBS, tap sideways or gently flick to remove excess buffer.
Circle each tissue sample on the slide with a hydrophobic barrier pen and place the slide in a wet‑chamber.
If multiple samples are on the slide, add a small amount of TBS to prevent drying during barrier creation.
Repeat the above for all slides.
When all tissues are circled, tap or flick to remove residual TBS and add 100 µL blocking buffer to each sample (process slides one at a time).
Incubate the slides for 1 h at room temperature in the wet‑chamber, ensuring the material never dries out.

steps.title: Incubate primary antibody
steps.instruction: Prepare antibody mix and incubate slides overnight at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Prepare the antibody mix: fill up to the final volume with antibody diluent.
If using a large panel or many antibodies, use the 2× aliquots to avoid excessive dilution; adjust with TBS so the mix reaches the correct final concentration.
Add enough antibody mix to cover each tissue (50 µL per sample).
Close the wet‑chamber and move it to a 4 °C incubator.
Ensure the incubation chamber is completely level to prevent drying.
Incubate the slides overnight.

steps.title: Apply Ir‑intercalator and final washes
steps.instruction: Treat slides with Ir‑intercalator, wash, dry, and store.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve the wet‑chamber from the 4 °C incubator.
Tap sideways or gently flick each slide and place it in TBS using the tray and slideholder specific for the slide‑wash robot.
Fill the wash‑station cuvettes with TBS and start the program "TBSwash".
During the wash, prepare Ir‑intercalator solution (50 µL per sample).
Incubate the slides with the Ir‑intercalator solution for 5 min in the wet‑chamber.
Wash the slides three times for 5 min each in TBS (as performed in the previous wash step).
Briefly dip the stained slides in ddH₂O.
Dry the slides under a gentle airflow.
Store the dried, stained slides in a box at room temperature.
